author: homer
title: Odyssey
summary: Twenty-four books on the homecoming of Odysseus in the tenth year after the fall of Troy: his son's search for news of him, his release from Calypso and his stay among the Phaeacians, the tale of his wanderings, and his return to Ithaca and his revenge on the suitors.

1.title: Athena Visits Telemachus
1.greek: Θεῶν ἀγορά, Ἀθηνᾶς παραίνεσις πρὸς Τηλέμαχον, Μνηστήρων εὐωχία
1.summary: The poet calls on the Muse to tell of Odysseus. In the tenth year after Troy he is held by Calypso, and while Poseidon is away among the Ethiopians the gods resolve to bring him home. Athena goes to Ithaca in the likeness of Mentes, finds the suitors feasting in Odysseus' house, and urges Telemachus to call an assembly and sail to Pylos and Sparta for news of his father. Penelope asks Phemius to stop his song of the Achaeans' homecoming; Telemachus rebukes her and the suitors, and lies awake all night pondering his journey.

2.title: The Assembly of the Ithacans
2.summary: At dawn Telemachus calls the first assembly in Ithaca since Odysseus sailed and accuses the suitors before the people. Antinous blames Penelope and her trick of the web; Zeus sends two eagles, which the seer Halitherses reads as a sign that Odysseus is near, and Mentor rebukes the silent Ithacans, but the suitors refuse to leave. Athena, in the likeness of Mentor, promises Telemachus a ship and a crew; Eurycleia fills jars and bags for the voyage, and at nightfall he sails for Pylos with the goddess beside him.

3.title: At Pylos
3.summary: Telemachus and Athena, in the likeness of Mentor, reach Pylos as the Pylians sacrifice black bulls to Poseidon on the shore, and Nestor's son Peisistratus welcomes them. Nestor knows nothing of Odysseus, but he tells of the quarrel of the sons of Atreus and the homecomings of the Achaeans, of how Aegisthus won Clytemnestra and killed Agamemnon while Menelaus wandered as far as Egypt, and of Orestes' vengeance, and he urges Telemachus to go on to Menelaus. Athena leaves in the likeness of a sea eagle, and Nestor knows the goddess. The next morning he sacrifices to her a heifer with gilded horns, his daughter Polycaste bathes Telemachus, and Telemachus and Peisistratus drive by way of Pherae toward Sparta.

4.title: At Lacedaemon
4.summary: Telemachus and Peisistratus reach Sparta during a double wedding and are welcomed by Menelaus, who has gathered his wealth in eight years of wandering while his brother was murdered. Helen recognizes Odysseus' son, puts an Egyptian drug against grief into the wine, and tells how Odysseus entered Troy disguised as a beggar; Menelaus tells how Odysseus held the chieftains silent in the Wooden Horse. The next day Menelaus tells how, becalmed off Egypt, he seized Proteus, the Old Man of the Sea, and learned of the deaths of Ajax and Agamemnon, of Odysseus held by Calypso, and of his own destiny in the Elysian plain. In Ithaca the suitors discover the voyage and send a ship to ambush Telemachus on his way home; Penelope prays to Athena, and the goddess comforts her in a dream with a phantom of her sister Iphthime.

5.title: The Raft of Odysseus
5.summary: At a second council of the gods Athena pleads again for Odysseus, and Zeus sends Hermes to Calypso's island with the command that he be let go. Calypso protests at the jealousy of the gods but yields, and swears by the water of Styx that she plans him no harm; Odysseus refuses her offer of immortality and chooses his mortal wife and his home. In four days he builds a raft, and on the fifth he sails, steering by the stars. On the eighteenth day, within sight of the Phaeacians' land, Poseidon wrecks him with a storm; Ino, now the sea goddess Leucothea, gives him her immortal veil, and after two nights and two days in the sea he struggles ashore at the mouth of a river, prays to its god, and falls asleep under a heap of leaves between two olive bushes.
